clues: This town sits in the Thames Valley, west of London in England. It lies where three big roads cross near each other.
This part of the Thames Valley has the warmest summer days in all of the British Isles. Rain here is low for the land as well.
Since the 1920s, folks have come here from all parts of the land and world to find work. Their mix helped make it a trade town.
Past London, no town in this land holds more head offices of world firms. Big names base their chief work here in town.
Its Trading Estate is the largest work estate in Europe held by one owner. That one site holds four hundred firms in all.
